intro: Uzbekistan is one of only two doubly landlocked countries in the world, with deserts, river oases and mountains in the east.

chapters.title: Deserts and oases
text: The Kyzylkum desert covers the centre. Life clusters along the Amu Darya and Syr Darya rivers and in the fertile Fergana Valley, shared with Kyrgyzstan and Tajikistan.
To be doubly landlocked means every neighbour is landlocked too; the only other such country is Liechtenstein.

chapters.title: The Aral Sea
text: The Aral Sea was once the world's fourth-largest lake. Most of it has dried up, leaving ships stranded in the desert.

keyTerms.meaning: A fertile spot in a desert with water.
